design: Final-build same-image regression rerun of all 72 distinct photographs preselected and labeled for the November 16 rehearsal rounds. Ten Food-101 categories outside the original nine, three images per class per round, class offsets 173-175 then 176-178; 12 separate Commons meal photographs with targets frozen before the original inference. No images added, removed or substituted after final predictions.

scoring.single_top1: The main API response dish_name equals its single reference after normalization; do not credit arbitrary regional alternatives as first-choice identification.
scoring.single_top3: The reference appears in main-response ranked_guesses[:3]; these are alternatives to one identification, not three separate dishes.
scoring.primary_set: Set of primary dish_name values in response dishes; matched, missed and extra scored independently.
scoring.mixed_recall: Matched primary targets / all predeclared target dishes; all-target-photo rate is separate.
scoring.extras: Suggestions outside the scored target set; some visible accompaniments were explicitly unscored, so these counts are not full ground-truth precision.
scoring.normalization: Lowercase alphanumeric word tokens with whitespace collapse; alias-aware results use only the frozen aliases above.
scoring.errors: HTTP failures count as empty predictions; never remove failed cases from denominators.

execution: Unchanged Flask /api/recognize with locally supplied official CLIP assets. Only get_clip asset resolution is replaced; model and processor remain pretrained and inference rules are unmodified.
limitations: Previously evaluated fixed photographs; a same-image regression rerun, not new independent or unseen test data.
Top-three candidate coverage is not automatic first-choice identification accuracy.
No user-selection success, browser interaction, production latency or overall real-world food accuracy is established.
The two original rounds have separate source images, with 60 single-dish and 12 mixed-meal photos in total.
